title: Hydra: Scale-out FHE Accelerator Architecture for Secure Deep Learning on FPGA
problem: Existing FHE accelerators for deep learning focus on single-node throughput by stacking parallelized compute clusters, which cannot leverage application-level parallelism across model layers and are not scalable beyond a single card for increasingly large models.
motivation: Privacy-preserving deep learning inference under Fully Homomorphic Encryption is computationally intensive (ciphertext convolution, matrix multiplication, bootstrapping), and single-node FPGA designs hit a performance ceiling that multi-node scale-out can overcome.
method: Hydra partitions the deep learning model (CNN and LLM layers) across multiple FPGA-based server nodes, each handling a portion of the model governed by a central scheduling mechanism on the host server. The architecture supports multi-server scaling with theoretically arbitrary numbers of compute nodes, enabling pipeline parallelism at the model level in addition to intra-node parallelism. Hydra achieves scale-out by distributing ciphertext operations across nodes with the host managing data routing and synchronization.
key_novelty: A scale-out multi-FPGA architecture for FHE-based deep learning inference that exploits application-level model parallelism rather than simply stacking parallelized single-card designs.
contributions: Scale-out FHE acceleration architecture supporting arbitrary numbers of FPGA compute nodes governed by a central scheduler
Up to 74x and 160x speedup over single-card SOTA FHE accelerators (Poseidon, FAB)
12-21x speedup over 8-card FAB-2 for FHE-based CNNs and LLMs
8.1x and 2.5x speedup over SOTA ASIC accelerators CraterLake and SHARP for LLM OPT-6.7B
